sections.kicker: Prepared for RISE Commercial District by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: RISE describes the space well and says very little about why a business would grow here and not next door.
sections.keep: The tenant stories. A window company, a salon and an air sealing firm in one place is a real picture of who RISE is for.

pins.quote: Easy business space for growing companies
pins.what: The headline names a category and an audience.
pins.why: Any landlord with a warehouse could use it, and the brand name does not appear in it.
pins.how: Say what RISE does for a tenant that a building owner does not.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: A growing company comparing three listings sees the same sentence three times.

pins.quote: Stop juggling the building. Start running your business.
pins.what: The second line is the sharpest thing on the page and it sits in small grey type.
pins.why: It is a point of view about what a tenant should not have to worry about.
pins.how: Move it up and let it lead.
pins.label: Your subhead
pins.cost: Your best sentence is read last.

pins.what: The real tenants appear as small video cards at the edge of the page.
pins.why: They are the only evidence that is specific to RISE, and a hair salon next to a warehouse shows range no brochure can.
pins.how: Give the tenants room to become the face of the brand.
pins.label: Your tenant cards
pins.cost: The most distinctive proof is cropped by the edge of the screen.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on RISE Commercial District's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Mailchimp, from another category. It treats small business owners as the heroes and its voice shows it.
